record.paper_title: Some open problems on Feynman periods
record.context_brief: Absence of ζ(2) from graph periods
record.original_question: Does ζ(2) fail to occur as a period of every Feynman graph G? In other words, is it true for all graphs G that the period space Pc(G) does not contain ζ(2)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. ζ (2) is not a period of any graph: ζ (2) ∈/ Pc(G).
In fact, while ζ (12) is known to appear in periods [39], the even zeta values with lower weight have not been observed as periods of any graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a connected Feynman graph (in massless scalar φ⁴ theory) that is primitive logarithmically divergent: G has 2N edges and N+1 independent cycles (so its first Symanzik/Kirchhoff polynomial Ψ_G is homogeneous of degree N+1 in the edge variables, and the integral below is logarithmically convergent and projective). Define the Feynman period of G by the convergent projective integral

  P(G) = ∫_{[0,∞)^{2N}} (1/Ψ_G(α_1,…,α_{2N})^2) · Ω,

where α_{2N} is set to 1 (or, equivalently, modded out by the projective scaling) and Ω = dα_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dα_{2N-1}. Let Pc(G) ⊂ ℂ denote the ℚ-vector space generated by the period P(G) together with all of its “motivic” cousins, i.e. all numbers obtainable as periods of the mixed Hodge structure on the relative cohomology of the graph hypersurface {Ψ_G = 0} that controls P(G).

Let ζ(2) = π²/6 = Σ_{n≥1} 1/n². Prove or disprove the following statement:

  For every connected primitive log-divergent Feynman graph G, ζ(2) ∉ Pc(G).

Equivalently, no Feynman period space Pc(G) of any such graph contains ζ(2).
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is a conjecture in the study of Feynman periods (sometimes attributed to the Brown–Schnetz/coaction-principle circle of ideas): even zeta values of low weight, in particular ζ(2), have not been observed as periods of any graph, while higher-weight zetas such as ζ(11) and even ζ(12) are known to occur. Recent surveys and computational work by Panzer, Schnetz and collaborators continue to list this as a conjecture without a proof or counterexample, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Feynman periods: graph structure and c2 invariant (Panzer/Schnetz talk)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists conjectures on which numbers occur as φ⁴ periods; ζ(2) is conjectured to be absent.
status_evidence.claim: The non-occurrence of ζ(2) as a graph period is presented as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Modular forms in quantum field theory (Brown–Schnetz)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the structure of the space of Feynman periods and which (motivic) zeta values appear.
status_evidence.claim: Even zeta values of low weight have not been found among Feynman periods, supporting the conjectural status.

status_evidence.title: Further investigations into the graph theory of φ⁴-periods and the c₂ invariant
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigation of φ⁴ periods continues to treat the absence of ζ(2) as conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: No proof or counterexample to the ζ(2) conjecture is reported in recent literature.
